Definition: from a derivative of G1364 and G4714; disunion, i.e. (figuratively) dissension:--division, sedition.
BiblicalUsage: Divisions are the splits that tear a church apart, and Paul names them among the works of the flesh. He warns the Romans to mark those who cause divisions contrary to the doctrine learned, and he lists them with hatred, wrath, and strife.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe divisions are a work of the flesh, not of the Spirit; the Spirit makes one body, and those who split it for their own doctrine or pride are working against Him, whatever they claim.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
